page: Google Cloud Platform h4d-highmem-192 is an x86_64 architecture cloud instance providing 192 dedicated vCPUs alongside 1488 GB of system memory. Operating within the high-memory tier of the h4d series, it delivers a dense allocation of 7.75 GB of RAM per dedicated vCPU, catering to large-scale computational tasks that require substantial volatile memory.

The instance does not include bundled local storage, meaning stateful operations depend on remote network-attached block storage volumes. It also contains no GPUs and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. This architecture deliberately isolates processor concurrency and memory capacity from peripheral accelerators and integrated drive controllers.

In terms of qualitative cost efficiency, provisioning 192 dedicated cores with nearly 1.5 TB of memory allows significant resource consolidation, minimizing multi-node communication overhead for memory-bound tasks. The h4d-highmem-192 is tailored for large in-memory databases, extensive caching tiers, large-scale batch processing, and memory-intensive data analytics pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform h4d-highmem-192 is an enterprise compute instance featuring 192 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 architecture and 1488 GB of total system RAM, providing an allocation of 7.75 GB per core. The server includes no GPUs and zero bundled local disk storage, relying entirely on network-attached storage for persistent data requirements. By omitting local disks and hardware accelerators, host resources are concentrated purely on dedicated compute throughput and high-capacity volatile memory. This hardware profile enables efficient consolidation of massive datasets into memory without the synchronization penalties of multi-node clustering. The instance is suited for large-scale in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, data engineering pipelines, and memory-intensive enterprise analytics workloads.
